title: January Protests: Matin Shabani Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Matin Shabani has been sentenced to death. The sentence was issued by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge. The verdict, which was communicated to Mr. Shabani in prison some time ago, sentenced him to death on charges including moharebeh (enmity against God) through participation in the destruction of public property and setting fire to religious centers, as well as assembly and collusion against the country.

A source familiar with the case confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “During the protests on January 8 and 9, 2026, in Shandiz, a mosque and a Dar al-Quran (Quranic education center) caught fire, and a case was opened in connection with these incidents.”

Matin Shabani was arrested in Shandiz during the nationwide January protests, along with six other citizens who were detained separately. After some time, he was transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Background of the January 2026 Protests

title: Four Citizens Arrested, Several Others Summoned Over Publication of Religious Content
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the Judiciary’s Media Center announced that a judicial case had been opened in connection with religious activities on social media and that four citizens had been arrested in this regard.

According to the report, four members of a group known as “Asma Academy” have been formally charged with “promotional activities contrary to the sacred laws of Islam through making baseless and false claims in religious matters,” and detention orders have been issued against them. Several other individuals affiliated with the group have also been summoned by judicial authorities for questioning.

The Judiciary’s Media Center claimed that members of the group, in collaboration with several social media activists and with the aim of generating income, had produced and published religious content, created podcasts, offered educational courses and packages, and organized both in-person and online seminars and workshops.

title: One Prisoner Executed at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, one prisoner was executed at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged on Tuesday, November 3, as Ali Shacheri (Bani-Turuf), 48, and a resident of Ahvaz.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the prisoner was arrested approximately five years ago after committing a murder during a dispute and physical altercation. He was subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

At the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.

title: Kaveh Othmani Arrested in Baneh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Kaveh Osmani has been arrested in Baneh County.

According to the report, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, agents of the Ministry of Intelligence arrested Kaveh Othmani at his family home without presenting a judicial warrant. Following his arrest, he was transferred to one of the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facilities in Sanandaj.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for Othmani’s arrest or the charges brought against him.

Kaveh Othmani, 56, is a resident of Khajamir Village in Baneh County, located in Kurdistan province.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Kaveh Osmani has been arrested in Baneh County.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January Protests: Another Protester Sentenced to Death Identified in Mashhad
content:
According to HRANA, Vahid Khodrikhah, 34, a resident of Mashhad, has been identified as another of the three individuals sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests in the city.

Vahid Khodrikhah, along with Matin Farnian, 23, and another individual, was sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, on the charge of “moharebeh” (enmity against God).

HRANA had previously reported the issuance of death sentences against these three individuals. However, at that time, only Matin Farnian’s identity had been confirmed. With the identification of Vahid Khodrikhah, the identities of two defendants in the case have now been established, while efforts to identify the third individual are ongoing.

An informed source told HRANA regarding Khodrikhah’s physical condition: “Before his arrest, he was wounded by gunfire during the January protests. The bullet has since been removed from his body, and the necessary follow-up medical care has been provided during his imprisonment.”
snippet: According to HRANA, Vahid Khodrikhah, 34, a resident of Mashhad, has been identified as another of the three individuals sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests in the city.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Amirhossein Mousavi Sentenced to Death and Imprisonment
content:
According to HRANA, Amirhossein Mousavi has been sentenced to imprisonment and death.

A source close to Mousavi’s family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Today, Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the verdict issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, was communicated to Mr. Mousavi. Under the ruling, he has been sentenced to five years in prison on the charge of ‘insulting religious sanctities’ and to death on the charge of ‘corruption on earth.’”

On September 21, 2026, the third hearing on the charges against Amirhossein Mousavi was held at the same court.

The second hearing was held in July 2026, while the first hearing took place on November 2, 2025, at Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati.
snippet: According to HRANA, Amirhossein Mousavi has been sentenced to imprisonment and death.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Revolutionary Court in Kerman Sentences Three Baha’i Citizens to Eight Years in Prison Each
content:
According to HRANA, citing IranWire, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour have been sentenced to a combined 24 years in prison.

According to the report, on October 31, 2026, Branch 5 of the Revolutionary Court of Kerman issued verdicts against these Baha’i citizens on charges including “membership in a group,” “assembly and collusion,” and “propaganda against the regime.” Under the rulings, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour were each sentenced to eight years in prison.

In connection with the same case, two other Baha’i citizens, Peyvand Naeimi and Borna Naeimi, have also been sentenced to a combined total of more than 24 years in prison.

Shakila Ghasemi was released from Kerman Prison on bail on August 15, 2026. She had previously been arrested by security forces at her residence in Kerman on February 2, 2026.

Adib Shahbazpour was arrested by security forces on January 18, 2026, in connection with nationwide protests, while Venus Hosseini-Nejad was arrested on January 15 of the same year. Both were subsequently released on bail.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing IranWire, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour have been sentenced to a combined 24 years in prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Retired Teacher Ali Ahmadi Beaten at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher from Nurabad Mamasani, was beaten by an official at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz.

A source close to Ahmadi’s family confirmed the incident to HRANA, stating: “On Sunday, November 1, Mr. Ahmadi was beaten by a prison official for unknown reasons while following up on medical treatment for his eye condition, despite having authorization to see a doctor. As a result, he sustained injuries to his head, face, nose, and back.”

The source further added: “In addition to his eye problems and a history of two surgical procedures involving his eye and prostate, Mr. Ahmadi also suffers from heart and kidney diseases. Nevertheless, prison authorities continue to prevent his transfer to medical facilities outside the prison.”

Previously, the Fars Teachers’ Trade Association reported that Ahmadi suffers from heart and kidney diseases. Furthermore, on September 1, 2026, despite a physician’s determination that he required medical care at facilities outside the prison, prison authorities, fully aware of his medical condition, prevented his transfer to a medical center.
snippet: According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher from Nurabad Mamasani, was beaten by an official at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: 25 Citizens Arrested in Bam Over Social Media Posts
content:
According to HRANA News Agency, citing ISNA, 25 citizens have been arrested in Bam County.

On Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor of Bam County announced the arrests, claiming that the individuals had been detained on charges of “disturbing public opinion” by publishing what he described as “false information, fabricated news, and rumors” on social media.

Hamid Hassaninia further stated that the individuals had been identified and arrested following continuous monitoring and surveillance of online activities by officers of the Cyber Police (FATA) in Bam County.

According to the judicial official, legal cases have been opened against all 25 arrested citizens.

The report provides no information regarding the identities of those arrested, their places of detention, or the specific content of the posts that led to their arrests.
snippet: According to HRANA News Agency, citing ISNA, 25 citizens have been arrested in Bam County.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Report on the Execution of a Juvenile Offender in Dezful and Two Other Prisoners in Isfahan
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, two prisoners were executed on Wednesday morning, October 21, 2026, in Isfahan Central Prison.

The prisoners have been identified as Mobarak Mohammadi, 43, and Ghasem Molla Amini, 49, both Afghan nationals from the city of Sheberghan.

According to the report, the two prisoners had been sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court in a joint case involving drug-related charges. An informed source stated that they had been arrested approximately two years earlier on a road leading to Isfahan on charges of transporting drugs.

The source further stated that Mobarak Mohammadi was the father of four children, while Ghasem Molla Amini was the father of three. The two men were related and had been living with their families in the city of Mashhad.

Juvenile Offender Executed in Dezful

In a separate report, Iran Human Rights Organization stated that a juvenile offender was executed in Dezful Prison on August 19, 2026.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, two prisoners were executed on Wednesday morning, October 21, 2026, in Isfahan Central Prison.

title: Three Citizens Arrested by IRGC Intelligence Agents in Asadabad
content:
According to HRANA, three citizens have been arrested in Asadabad. HRANA has verified the identities of the detainees as Javad Kouhi, Keyumars Heydari, and a citizen identified by the surname Rostami (first name unknown), all residents of Asadabad, located in Hamadan Province.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the three citizens were arrested at their residences by IRGC Intelligence agents on the evening of Sunday, November 1, 2026.

A source familiar with the case and close to the detainees’ families confirmed the arrests to HRANA, stating that the individuals face charges of “spreading false information” in connection with managing a Telegram channel and publishing content on it.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the detainees’ whereabouts.
snippet: According to HRANA, three citizens have been arrested in Asadabad. HRANA has verified the identities of the detainees as Javad Kouhi, Keyumars Heydari, and a citizen identified by the surname Rostami

title: January Protests: Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the death sentences of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, two defendants in the case known as the “Ali Khani Square case” in Isfahan, were carried out this morning.

The Judiciary’s Media Center has claimed that four law enforcement officers were killed during the protests on January 8, 2026, in Ali Khani Square in Isfahan. The institution also alleged that a number of protesters attacked law enforcement officers and damaged public buildings and property.

In outlining the charges against Amirhossein Ebrahimi, Mizan claimed that he was present in Ali Khani Square on the day of the incident and, while carrying a bladed weapon, participated in the destruction of public property and the assault of law enforcement officers. According to the report, Mr. Ebrahimi went into hiding at a relative’s home following the incident and was subsequently arrested along with his brother.

title: January 2026 Protests: Alireza Dowlati and Mohammad Khalizadeh Sentenced to a Combined 35 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Alireza Dowlati and Mohammad Khalizadeh have been sentenced to prison. Based on information obtained by HRANA, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced Mohammad Khalizadeh to 30 years in prison on charges of “moharebeh” (enmity against God) and Alireza Dowlati to five years in prison on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security.”

A source familiar with the case and close to the families of the two men confirmed the news to HRANA, stating that Dowlati and Khalizadeh are co-defendants in the same case as Omran Amani, a prisoner who has been sentenced to death.

The three men, who had been living together in the same house, were arrested in Tehran on February 11, 2026, in connection with the nationwide protests. All three are currently held in Greater Tehran Prison.

title: Two Women Sentenced to 22 Years in Prison Each in Connection with January Protests
content:
According to HRANA, two women have been sentenced to prison on charges of “espionage” in a case related to the nationwide protests of January 2026.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced each woman to 22 years in prison. HRANA has not yet been able to verify the identities of the two prisoners, and efforts to establish their identities are ongoing. Both women are currently serving their sentences in Qarchak Prison in Varamin.

A source familiar with the case told HRANA: “The two women initially faced the death penalty, but the judge ultimately granted leniency and sentenced each of them to 22 years in prison.”

The two women are co-defendants in the same case as three other individuals: Amirreza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and Mehdi Jalali, a cleric and former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). All three men have been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.
snippet: According to HRANA, two women have been sentenced to prison on charges of “espionage” in a case related to the nationwide protests of January 2026.

title: January 2026 Protests: Amir Delshad Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Amir Delshad, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge, sentenced Delshad to death on charges including carrying out operations detrimental to national security and interests on behalf of an opposition group through active participation in the January 2026 protests, as well as setting fire to and destroying public property.

An informed source told HRANA regarding the latest developments in Delshad’s case: “Amir Delshad’s appeal has been registered with the Supreme Court.”

Amir Delshad was arrested by security forces during the January 2026 protests and is currently held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Background of the January 2026 Protests
